candidates: When adding width-responsive layout changes to a component (e.g. hiding a label or switching flex direction at narrow widths), implement them primarily with a container query inside an `@supports (container-type: inline-size)` block, and include the equivalent `@media` rule only as a fallback for browsers that lack container query support. Avoid gating `flex-direction` changes exclusively on a viewport media query: at viewport widths where the component's container is wider or narrower than the viewport, this produces broken intermediate layouts that a container query would handle correctly.

When a button label must be hidden visually at small sizes (e.g. to show only an icon), do not use `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or omit the text node — screen readers will fail to announce the button's purpose. Instead, apply `srOnlyStyles` (exported from `storybook/theming`, defined in `code/core/src/theming/global.ts`) to the text `<span>` so the label is visually hidden but still read aloud by assistive technology.
